value.body: A two-year master's in anthropology, offered as an M.A. or an M.Sc. depending on the university. Students usually specialise in social-cultural or biological (physical) anthropology, and some programmes offer archaeological or forensic anthropology. Fieldwork and a dissertation are a standard part of the course.

items.label: PG students in Anthropology
items.note: All PG programmes in the subject
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 13, actual responses (Ministry of Education)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, usually with anthropology (some universities accept graduates in other social or life sciences). Central and many state universities admit through CUET-PG; others hold their own entrance test or admit on graduation marks.

value.title: At a glance
items: A small field with few seats, concentrated in a limited number of universities.
Research and teaching posts usually need UGC-NET or a Ph.D. as well.
Fieldwork skills also lead to development-sector, social-research and market-research work.

value.title: PG students in Anthropology
value.note: AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year, so part of any change may reflect reporting rather than real growth or decline. PG level covers M.A. and M.Sc. together; Ph.D. and M.Phil. are excluded.
